quotes.how: parsed with the same routine scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs uses, extracted into this file and run over the resolved intent, so every criterionText is the intent's own text: the 6 criteria it declares are ["SC1","SC2","SC3","SC4","SC5","SC6"] and scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs compares them character for character

why: No row is required, and the list therefore names no driver, no instance and no verdict path: scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs refuses a list with no required row that names a driver, so naming one would be the opposite defect.

The reason is not convenience. A required row must name the driver a control-ai-browsers run expression takes to the wave gate, and that driver must return the gate's four readings - toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext - with the required rows together citing drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext. Every fact these six criteria are written about is a reading of this repository's own gate: 158 .project reference(s) in 141 suite(s), 6 claim(s) held against a range, 12 check stages, 1 recorded NavigationSkipped entry, 4 driven check runs and the diff of 199 suite(s) against d94502d1. None of them is an element's rect or a dev context, so naming a driver would make the gate return a page reading for a claim about the gate.

The portal is not lost by that ruling: it is the page the four defects were measured on and every reason names the clause that would have made a row required. Each row cites the artefact that carries it, the reading it carries and the commands that prove it.

capture.reading: an armed run re-derives the list from the intent this checkout binds, the measurements it cites and the files it names, and writes it only when a value moved; a default run reads the file and asserts it is exactly what this head derives.

claims.criterionText: A committed test that resolves a `.project/` path the milestone's own archive move deletes fails the ship gate, naming the file and the path; a milestone whose tests reference no such path passes the same check.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause reaches a criterion when an insurance-portal route can produce its facts, and this one's fact is whether a committed suite opens a `.project` path the milestone's own archive move deletes - a property of this repository's test tree and of the ship flow that moves it, which no route of any page carries. The gate's one `control-ai-browsers run` driver returns an element's toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext readings, none of which can say what a suite opens, so a portal-backed verdict would name a driver that cannot carry the answer. The portal is the page the defect was found beside, not the surface that can prove the check fires.

claims.criterionText: A task log claiming a file change absent from the milestone's range fails the ship gate, naming the task and the file.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause asks for a portal-backed verdict where a portal route can produce the facts, and this criterion's facts are what `git diff --name-status` records for a milestone's own range beside what a task log claims - a reading of this repository's history that no inspected page produces and none could. The gate's one `control-ai-browsers run` driver returns an element's toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext readings; a range's changed paths are not among them, so a portal-backed row would name a driver that cannot carry a range at all. The portal is named here because it was considered: a portal drive would measure a page, not the diff a claim is held against.

claims.criterionText: The archive-path and fix-record checks run inside the gate rather than as advisory output, so neither defect can reach `ship/done` while the check is red.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause reaches a criterion only where a portal route produces its facts, and this one's fact is the order and the membership of `package.json`'s check chain: two stages run inside `npm run check` rather than beside a passing gate. A command list is not a page reading, so no route can produce it, and the gate's one `control-ai-browsers run` driver returns an element's toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext readings rather than a chain of commands. The portal is the subject the milestone's first defect was found in, and this criterion is about the gate that must refuse before the portal's page is ever served again.

claims.criterionText: A navigation terminal for an already-ended navigation id produces a finding naming the skipped navigation, proven by a pin fed from `research/raw/m041-navigation.json` rather than from a hand-built event list.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause makes a verdict required where an insurance-portal route can produce a criterion's facts, and this one's fact is a `NavigationSkipped` entry in a recorded stream whose id has already ended - the entry carries id 3 and url /claim/list in frame terminals.skip.events, with its start in ["superseded.events"] and not in its own frame. A portal route does emit navigation events, and the recording was taken from one, but the gate's one `control-ai-browsers run` driver reads an element's toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext and returns none of the router's stream, so no driver in this repository carries the facts a portal-backed verdict would have to cite. The portal is named because the recorded page was a real one; what proves the criterion is the recording and the pin fed from it.

claims.criterionText: Each check reddens a synthetic regression that reproduces its measured instance, and the failure names the file and the claim — proven by removing the synthetic regression and observing the check green again.
claims.reason: The charter's portal clause is answered rather than dodged: a portal route is an Angular page and could in principle produce a page reading, but this criterion's facts are a check's own behaviour under a synthetic regression - the archive-path instance exits 1 where its control exits 0, the fix-record instance exits 1 where its control exits 0, and what each printed is recorded - and no route produces that. The gate's one control-ai-browsers run driver returns an element's toolElements, drawnRect, descriptor and noDevContext readings, so a portal-backed row would make the gate return a rect for a claim about a mutant. The portal is the page the first defect was measured on; the evidence is the pair of runs and the mutants the checks ship.
